content: 1. Mefenamic acid is an analgesic medication approved by the FDA for the treatment of dysmenorrhea, low back pain, and general pain. 2. The drug carries a Black Box Warning, indicating significant risks associated with its use. 3. Common adverse reactions to mefenamic acid include edema and elevated liver function test results. 4. For adults, the initial recommended dose is 500 mg, followed by 250 mg every 6 hours as needed, typically not exceeding one week. For dysmenorrhea, treatment begins at the onset of bleeding and symptoms and continues for 2 to 3 days. 5. There is limited information on off-label uses of mefenamic acid in both adults and pediatric patients. 6. Mefenamic acid is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to the drug, those who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions to aspirin or other NSAIDs, and those with active gastrointestinal ulceration or chronic inflammation. 7. The drug is also contraindicated for peri-operative pain management in coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery and in patients with preexisting renal disease. 8. Cardiovascular risks include an increased likelihood of thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, which can be fatal. Patients with cardiovascular disease or risk factors should use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration. 9. NSAIDs, including mefenamic acid, can cause or worsen hypertension and may reduce the efficacy of antihypertensive medications like diuretics. 10. Fluid retention and edema have been observed in some patients taking NSAIDs, necessitating caution in those with heart failure or fluid retention. 11. Gastrointestinal risks include serious adverse events such as inflammation, bleeding, ulceration, and perforation, which can occur without warning. Patients with a history of peptic ulcer disease or gastrointestinal bleeding are at significantly higher risk. 12. Renal toxicity, including renal papillary necrosis, may occur with long-term NSAID use, particularly in patients with impaired renal function, heart failure, or liver dysfunction. Discontinuation of the drug usually leads to recovery. 13. Severe hepatic reactions, including jaundice, fulminant hepatitis, and liver failure, have been reported. Patients with symptoms of liver dysfunction should discontinue the drug and undergo evaluation. 14. Hematological effects, such as anemia, may occur due to fluid retention, gastrointestinal blood loss, or effects on erythropoiesis. Long-term users should have their hemoglobin or hematocrit levels monitored. 15. Mefenamic acid inhibits platelet aggregation and may prolong bleeding time, necessitating caution in patients with coagulation disorders or those on anticoagulants. 16. Patients with aspirin-sensitive asthma should avoid mefenamic acid due to the risk of severe bronchospasm. 17. Serious skin reactions, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. Patients should discontinue the drug at the first sign of rash or hypersensitivity. 18. 19. Trace amounts of mefenamic acid may be present in breast milk, and its use in nursing mothers should be carefully considered due to potential risks to the infant. 20. Safety and efficacy in pediatric patients under 14 years of age have not been established. 21. Elderly patients are at greater risk of adverse effects due to decreased renal function and should be treated with caution. 22. Mefenamic acid may interact with other drugs, including ACE inhibitors, aspirin, diuretics, lithium, methotrexate, and warfarin, potentially altering their efficacy or increasing the risk of adverse effects. 23. Overdose symptoms include lethargy, drowsiness, nausea, vomiting, and epigastric pain, which are generally reversible with supportive care. Severe cases may involve gastrointestinal bleeding, hypertension, renal failure, respiratory depression, or coma. 24. Mefenamic acid is a member of the fenamate group of NSAIDs and exhibits anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antipyretic properties. 25. The drug is available in capsules containing 250 mg of mefenamic acid for oral administration.
